analysis.title: Connecting the Dots: Sell-off, US Midterms, Data centers and Conviction List plus key research
key_insights: The initial US sell-off after the Democratic sweep at the Midterms spread beyond data center-related names to the index level. Owners of current compute were seen as relative beneficiaries of a data center slowdown because supply would be lower.

GS revisits an Aterio expert call on US data centers. Texas is 26% of 2026-2030 net additions to the US pipeline, and most of that pipeline is announced but not under construction. Michael Ng thinks his US data center forecasts are conservative.

Aterio's definition of under construction includes site works such as land clearing, which developers usually do before securing an electricity services agreement or environmental and air permits. A moratorium could therefore affect projects counted as under construction.

Alberto Gandolfi argues Europe has a significant data center opportunity and that investments should be judged idiosyncratically given execution risk. Solaria is a potential European beneficiary, Buy rated and on the Conviction List, with a CMD on 19 Nov in London.

November Conviction List changes. Europe adds Carlsberg and Deutsche Bank and removes Haleon, HSBC and CTP. US adds Amphenol. APAC adds Elite Material, Yokohama Rubber and JSW Steel and removes NYPCB, Shengyi Tech and Hong Kong Exchanges.

GS looks for upside to consensus earnings in Conviction List selection. Carlsberg was added for topline growth from soft drinks and deleveraging progress. Deutsche Bank was added for improving revenue momentum in Corporate and Private bank.
Rating changes: BAT upgraded to Buy and Imperial reiterated Buy, both with 22% price target upside. Kuehne & Nagel and Gecina cut to Neutral.

AI financing: $568 billion of AI-related issuance in global IG syndicated credit so far this year, including $40bn in the past several days. Hyperscaler lease commitments total $1.7tn, 75% of them for leases not yet started. Recent hyperscaler debt deals pushed supply above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250bn.
State-level capacity analysis shows Texas at 20% of 2027E and 27% of 2028E US data center net additions. Labor availability is a key constraint on AI and data center power demand growth.

European earnings: GS raises SXXP EPS growth forecasts to 18% for 2026 and 7% for 2027 and adds 5% for 2028, above economic growth because global growth matters more. US earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating.

Commodity forecast changes: Brent Dec26 raised to $105/bbl from $90 and 2027 average to $88 from $80 on supply disruption risk. End-2026 gold cut to $4,150/toz and end-2027 to $4,800/toz from $5,400 on the Fed's hawkish shift and positioning. Copper faces added Chile labor supply risk into 2027.

Binance disclosed a cybersecurity incident on 29 Oct, the largest to date by affected assets, with $19.9bn or 14% of assets leaving the platform. GS says it questions cybersecurity across crypto and could weigh on long-term industry growth.

Q3 results with big share moves: Maersk -6% (miss, revised guidance), Heidelberg Materials +10%, Weir -10%, Zalando -6%, Scout24 +7%, Ryanair +5%, Lufthansa +4%, Barry Callebaut +9%, Philips +5%, Bayer +4%, Lanxess +6%, Viridien +3%.

TMT: GS sees AMD revenue growth strong through 2027 versus lowered investor expectations. Arista beat on 3Q and raised 2026 guidance. Apple beat on iPhone and Mac revenue but memory and inference costs pressure gross margins.

Legrand beat and raised, with 9M26 data center growth around 40% versus over 30% at 1H26, implying FY26 consensus rises by a low single-digit percent. Rheinmetall cut guidance on delayed Arminius awards, implying cuts of about 5% to FY26 consensus sales and 8% to operating earnings.
BOE hiked on Thursday as expected. GS forecasts another hike in February, with December possible, and sees risks to its two-hike baseline skewed toward more tightening, above market pricing.

Fiscal and China macro: GS sees a roughly neutral fiscal impulse in 2027 with deficit-driven downside risks to growth. China's domestic weakness is driven by persistent fiscal tightening and leadership does not want a property rebound.

Consumer and healthcare calls: LVMH Buy on the F&L division, AstraZeneca Buy on 2027 catalysts, Essity and Magnum Ice Cream reiterated Sell on cost inflation, Novo Neutral with FY27 seen as a transition year.

market_movers.rationale: Upgraded to Buy with 22% price target upside on defensive nicotine qualities and best-in-class margins. New Categories growth is accelerating.
Imperial Brands reiterated Buy with 22% price target upside.
Kuehne & Nagel cut to Neutral with unchanged target. Shares outperformed and the gap to consensus has narrowed.
Gecina cut to Neutral after lower forecasts. GSe 27/28 EPS are 3-4% below Visible Alpha consensus.
Solaria is Buy rated and on the Conviction List, a potential European data center beneficiary with a CMD on 19 Nov.
Added to the US Conviction List.
Carlsberg added to the European Conviction List for solid topline growth from soft drinks and deleveraging progress.
Deutsche Bank added to the European Conviction List on improving revenue momentum in Corporate and Private bank and exposure to German momentum.
GS sees strong revenue growth through 2027, with data center underpinning growth despite PC headwinds.
Beat on EPS, revenue and margin in 3Q with 2026 revenue growth of 48% YoY at the midpoint and a strong 2027 outlook.
iPhone and Mac revenue beat shows pricing power. Memory and inference costs weigh on the outlook and gross margins.
In-line 3Q with faster organic growth but lower margins. Focus shifts to the CMD and new mid-term targets.
Maersk down to Sell. Container market seen as at peak, with 3Q miss and higher costs.
Drax rose 7% on a strategic partnership for a data center of more than 1GW. CMD on 23 Nov is the next catalyst.
Merlin Properties remains focused on its data center programme in Lisbon. Spanish regulatory risk has reduced.
RWE won 2GW across three gas plants, with another auction in December and a rich catalyst path.
Legrand beat and raised. Data center growth was about 40% over 9M26.
Rheinmetall cut guidance on delayed Arminius awards. Rated Buy and on the Conviction List.
Nordex results point to further consensus upgrades. GSe margin 12.3% versus consensus 11%.
Heidelberg Materials rose 10% on 9% EBIT growth, a 3% beat versus consensus, with cost savings and pricing power intact.
Saudi Aramco beat on net income with strong cash flow generation.
Lufthansa reduced the top end of guidance. GS expects consensus in the lower half of the range.
Lanxess implied 4Q looks demanding on normal seasonality despite narrowed FY guidance.
Alstom numbers cut materially after a profit warning. EV/Sales is 0.36 versus a 0.17x trough.
Essity has constrained pricing power that leaves margins vulnerable to cost inflation.
Magnum Ice Cream faces cost inflation weighing on 2027 margin expansion and volume growth.
Halma is on the Conviction List. At a 10-year median P/E of about 30x on ex-Photonics EPS the market values Photonics below 8x. GSe Photonics growth is +38% in FY27.
LVMH is optimistic on the F&L division as the LV brand transition becomes less of a headwind.
Valuation does not reflect the growth opportunity and several 2027 catalysts.
FY27 could be another transition year, with the ex-US Wegovy pill a possible upside driver.
Strong 3Q beat and raise supported by one-offs, phasing and cost control.
Omnicom is the main winner in Lidl's EU media account review.

sector_views.rationale: Europe has a significant data center opportunity and positioning looks better after the US Midterms. GS says investments should be judged idiosyncratically given execution risk.
Midterm outcome is likely positive overall for US renewable activity, including Orsted and EDPR.
GS sees the container market cooling in 2027 and downgraded Maersk to Sell and Kuehne & Nagel to Neutral.
Mixed results. IAG missed on disruption costs, Ryanair FY28E is 25% below consensus, Lufthansa cut the top of guidance.
Essity and Magnum Ice Cream rated Sell on margin pressure from cost inflation, while BAT is upgraded on defensive qualities.
Positive medium- to long-term NAND outlook after Kioxia read-across. Buy Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
European earnings growth is forecast above economic growth because global growth matters more.

earnings_insights: Arista 3Q: EPS, revenue and margin beat, 2026 revenue guidance raised to +48% YoY at the midpoint, strong initial 2027 outlook.
Apple fiscal Q: iPhone and Mac revenue beat. Gross margin pressured by memory cost inflation, partly offset by higher ASPs and inventory management.
AMD: GS sees strong revenue growth through 2027 versus investor expectations lowered after Intel's report last week.
IAG 3Q26: EBIT €1.73bn reported, 5% below company-compiled consensus of €1.81bn, partly from extra disruption costs.
Heidelberg Materials: 9% EBIT growth reported, a 3% beat versus consensus. Shares +10% on results.
Maersk 3Q: miss versus expectations with revised guidance, container volumes lower on congestion and weather, bunker and network costs higher. Shares -6%.
Ryanair: GSe FY27 net income raised slightly and 1% ahead of VA consensus, while FY28E is 25% below consensus as fuel prices are not fully in models. Shares +5%.
Legrand: 9M26 data center growth about 40% versus over 30% at 1H26, implying FY26 consensus rises by a low single-digit percent.
IMCD: organic gross profit growth 9.6% in 3Q26 versus 7.3% in 2Q26, with APAC at 20.1% versus 7% in 2Q.
Rheinmetall pre-release: guidance cut on Arminius project delays, implying about 5% cuts to FY26 consensus sales and 8% to operating earnings. 3Q profit beat.
Nordex: strong results as pre-released. GSe margin 12.3% versus consensus 11%.
Next: full price sales +8% YoY, international revenue +32%, marketing spend +67% YoY.
Sanofi 3Q: strong beat and raise, supported by one-offs, phasing and cost control.
GXO 3Q: in-line, faster organic growth acceleration with lower margins. GS expects limited consensus changes.
Lufthansa: solid 3Q, top end of guidance reduced, shares +4%. GS expects consensus in the lower half of the updated range.
Saudi Aramco: net income beat and strong cash flow generation.
US earnings: growth is strong but no longer accelerating, per Ben Snider.
Weir shares fell 10% on results because of soft organic order intake versus peers. Zalando fell 6% on broadly in-line results.
Upcoming dates: Halma FY results 19 Nov, Solaria CMD 19 Nov, Drax CMD 23 Nov, Marks & Spencer CMD next week.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects another hike in February, with December possible. Its two-hike baseline is below market pricing and risks tilt toward more tightening.
GS raised the forecast on high supply disruption risk.
Higher forecast on supply disruption risks.
Lowered because of the Fed's hawkish shift in recent months and its implications for positioning.
GS stays constructive longer term on structurally strong central bank demand.
Above economic growth because global growth matters more than domestic growth.
Issuance is accelerating in EUR IG and GS sees scope for it to continue. Supply is above the $250bn full-year forecast.
Confirms softening consumption momentum into winter.
Group-wide impulse roughly neutral, with expansion in Germany and Japan and consolidation in the UK.

crypto_views: Binance disclosed a cybersecurity incident on 29 Oct, the largest to date by affected assets. $19.9bn or 14% of assets have left the platform.
GS says the incident calls into question cybersecurity across the crypto ecosystem and could impact long-term industry growth (James Yaro).

risk_factors: US data center slowdown from permitting moratoria or power constraints, since most of the pipeline is announced but not under construction.
Execution risk on data center investments, especially in Europe.
Rising AI-related debt supply and off balance sheet hyperscaler lease commitments of $1.7tn.
Hawkish Fed and further BOE tightening risk.
Crypto exchange cybersecurity incidents, as at Binance.
Memory cost inflation pressuring hardware gross margins, for example Apple.
Supply disruption risk in oil and Chile copper labor negotiations.
Large deficits leave growth risks skewed to the downside.
Cost inflation hurting consumer staples margins.
Socialization risk at Vonovia and Berlin anti-socialisation draft rules.
vol_and_positioning: GS cut its gold forecasts on the implications of the Fed's hawkish shift for positioning.
Halma analysis: a 10-year median P/E of about 30x on ex-Photonics EPS implies the market prices Photonics below 8x.
Alstom EV/Sales is 0.36x versus a 0.17x trough, so the multiple is not at trough.
Luxury investors are cautious and many do not expect US demand to accelerate sequentially this quarter.
Share price reactions this season were large in both directions, for example Weir -10% and Heidelberg +10%, with some stocks falling after outperforming into results (Zalando).
geopolitical: US Midterms: Democrats won broadly (a 'blue tsunami'). GS flags implications for utilities, renewables and data center permitting.
Possible moratorium on US data center construction, which could affect projects counted as under construction.
Chile copper labor negotiations add a supply risk into 2027, most relevant for BHP, RIO, LUN and ANTO.
Coca-Cola HBC fell 18% on press reports that a local producer petitioned Russian authorities to put its Russian operations under external administration.
German defence spending is driving a pick-up in equipment investment.
China leadership has no desire to see a property rebound and must manage its large and rising trade surplus.
Supply disruption risks cited for oil, and uncertain supply for European gas (TTF).

tension_points.bull_case: Michael Ng thinks his US data center forecasts are conservative, and AI financing keeps flowing with $568 billion of IG issuance this year.
tension_points.bear_case: Most of the pipeline is announced and not under construction, Texas is 26% of 2026-2030 net additions, and a moratorium could hit projects counted as under construction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Permits or electricity services agreements failing to materialise for announced Texas projects, since site works are counted as under construction before those approvals.

tension_points.bull_case: Alberto Gandolfi argues Europe has a significant DC opportunity, as recent deals including Drax this week show.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors debate whether a US slowdown helps Europe, and GS says DC investments carry execution risk and should be judged idiosyncratically.

tension_points.bull_case: US earnings growth is strong and market breadth has partly widened through catch up and catch down.
tension_points.bear_case: Earnings growth is no longer accelerating, which is the fundamental challenge for equity investors.
